rows.question: Which three risk factors are most specific to this company's business (rather than generic to any public company)? Summarize each in one sentence.
rows.answer: (1) Box's success depends on widespread market adoption of cloud-based content management, since it derives substantially all revenue from this single product category, unlike diversified companies. (2) Because Box uses ratable subscription revenue recognition over one-month-to-three-year terms, declines in new/renewed bookings are masked for multiple quarters, delaying visibility into business deterioration. (3) Box carries $460.0 million in 2029 Convertible Notes that could require cash settlement or repurchase upon conversion or a fundamental change, and it may lack sufficient cash flow to meet these obligations.

citations.quote: Since we derive, and expect to continue to derive, substantially all of our revenue and cash flows from sales of our cloud content management solutions, our success will depend to a substantial extent on the widespread adoption of cloud computing in general and of cloud-based content management services in particular.
citations.section: Item 1A. RISK FACTORS

citations.quote: Consequently, a decline in new or renewed subscriptions in any one quarter may not be reflected in our revenue results for that quarter. However, any such decline will negatively affect our revenue in future quarters.
citations.section: Item 1A. RISK FACTORS

citations.quote: As of January 31, 2026, we had outstanding debt, including an aggregate principal amount of $460.0 million issued under the 2029 Convertible Notes.
citations.section: Item 1A. RISK FACTORS

citations.quote: we may not have sufficient cash flow from our business to settle conversions of our convertible notes in cash, repay the convertible notes at maturity, or repurchase the convertible notes as required following a fundamental change.
citations.section: Item 1A. RISK FACTORS

expected.text: Reference picks (judgment question; only citation support is scored): (1) Competition from much larger platform vendors - Microsoft (SharePoint/OneDrive), Google (Drive), OpenText and Dropbox - some of which bundle content products for free or at low prices in enterprise license deals, pressuring Box's pricing, with generative AI potentially reshaping the market. (2) Dependence on renewals and expansion: results hinge on customers renewing and upgrading (seat expansion, multi-product Suites such as Enterprise Advanced); net retention rate has fluctuated (104% at Jan 31, 2026 vs 102% a year earlier) amid budget scrutiny and partial churn. (3) Foreign-currency exposure concentrated in Japan: ~25% of revenue comes from Japanese customers and ~40% of revenue is in foreign-currency contracts, so yen weakness directly hurts reported results despite hedging. Other defensible company-specific picks: reliance on third-party public cloud hosting after migrating off its own data centers; rights and redemption obligations of the KKR-led Series A convertible preferred; AI-related risks.

rows.judge_reason: Each of the three claims is directly backed by the cited quotes.

rows.question: Is the board classified (staggered), and does the company have more than one class of common stock with different voting rights?
rows.answer: Yes, Box's board is classified: the certificate of incorporation and bylaws authorize 'a classified board of directors whose members serve staggered three-year terms,' and the FY2026 proxy confirms the Board is divided into three staggered classes with three-year terms (most recent Q2 FY2027 10-Q, filed 2026-08-26). However, these excerpts only reference 'Class A common stock' throughout and do not disclose the existence or voting rights of any other class of common stock (e.g., a Class B), so whether Box has multiple classes with different voting rights could not be confirmed from the provided excerpts.
rows.period: as of Q2 FY2027 (filed 2026-08-26); board structure corroborated by FY2026 DEF 14A (as of fiscal year ended January 31, 2026)

citations.quote: authorizing a classified board of directors whose members serve staggered three-year terms;
citations.section: Item 1A. RISK FACTORS

citations.quote: our Board of Directors is divided into three staggered classes of directors.
citations.section: proxy

citations.quote: Risks Related to Ownership of Our Class A Common Stock
citations.section: Item 1A. RISK FACTORS

expected.text: Yes, the board is classified: directors are divided into three staggered classes, each elected for three-year terms (Class III nominees in 2026 for terms to 2029). No multi-class common structure: Box has a single class of common stock (Class A, one vote per share; the former Class B common stock was retired in 2018). The only other voting security is the Series A Convertible Preferred Stock (KKR-led), which votes together with Class A on an as-converted basis and has certain separate class consent rights. MUST: classified/staggered board = yes; single class of common stock with one vote per share = no dual-class. OPTIONAL: the Series A preferred voting, the anti-takeover framing in risk factors.

rows.judge_reason: The classified board part matches, but the assistant failed to conclude that Box has a single class of common stock (no dual-class), leaving that required element unconfirmed.

rows.question: Has the company entered into a cooperation, nomination, or standstill agreement with an activist or other significant shareholder? If so, summarize the key terms.
rows.answer: The most recent filing (BOX 10-Q Q2 FY2027, filed 2026-08-26) does not disclose an activist cooperation, nomination, or standstill agreement. It instead describes the 2021 Investment Agreement with KKR-led investors, which originally gave KKR the right to designate one board nominee, but 'KKR has waived both its rights to designate or nominate an Investor Designee...to the Board and its preemptive rights pursuant to the Investment Agreement.' No separate activist cooperation/standstill agreement is mentioned in the excerpts.

citations.quote: KKR had the right to designate one candidate for nomination for election to our Board of Directors and preemptive rights to participate in certain future offering of securities of Box for so long as KKR and its permitted transferees maintained a minimum aggregate holdings of our stock as described in further detail in the Investment Agreement; however, KKR has waived both its rights to designate or nominate an Investor Designee (as defined in the Investment Agreement) to the Board and its preemptive rights pursuant to the Investment Agreement.
citations.section: Item 1A. RISK FACTORS

expected.text: No cooperation, settlement or standstill agreement with an activist investor is disclosed in any of the filings. The only related arrangement is the April 7, 2021 Investment Agreement with a KKR-led investor group (purchasers of $500 million of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock; KKR entities hold ~28.5% of the preferred): it gave KKR the right to designate one candidate for nomination to Box's Board (while KKR kept minimum holdings) plus preemptive rights, but KKR has since waived both its board-designation right and its preemptive rights (per the latest 10-Q). Holders of a majority of the Series A preferred must consent to certain actions (e.g., issuing senior/parity securities, special dividends above an agreed amount). MUST: say there is no activist cooperation/standstill agreement AND mention the KKR investment agreement's board nomination right and that it has been waived. An answer that only says 'none' without the KKR nuance is incomplete but directionally correct. Also correct: an answer stating that no activist cooperation/standstill agreement is disclosed (the question is ambiguous for Box; KKR is an investor, not an activist).

rows.judge_reason: Matches expected: no activist agreement, KKR board nomination right waived; quote supports all material claims.

rows.question: Is the company party to any material pending legal proceedings? If so, describe them.
rows.answer: No material legal proceedings are disclosed. As of the most recent 10-K (fiscal year ended January 31, 2026), Box states it is subject only to ordinary-course litigation and claims, and management believes there was not at least a reasonable possibility of a material loss from such contingencies.
